combo_props.existing_mechanism: A combo is a sum of correlated components; the mean is the sum of marginal means, while the variance depends on within-game covariance (minutes positive, role tradeoffs negative). Mispricing arises when a market prices combos as independent sums of the component lines, or when component prices update at different speeds after news. All single-stat drivers apply, with minutes and game script as common factors that dominate the tails.

season_futures_team.existing_mechanism: Probabilities come from a simulation: team ratings with uncertainty updated through the season, the remaining schedule with rest and home/away, injury scenarios for key players and the official tiebreaker/play-in structure; the playoffs add bracket path and series models with playoff-tightened rotations. Win-total and seed markets are sensitive to rating uncertainty and boundary effects; title odds are convex in star health. Market prices incorporate narratives; edges come from uncertainty handling, luck regression and rule boundaries.

existing_interactions.hypothesis: Usage matters only with minutes; the product drives all components together.
Higher pace raises all components but correlates rebounds and assists with scoring, widening the joint tail.
Blowout probability cuts milestone completion for stars more than for role players.

unreg:team_and_player_counting_specials.existing_mechanism: Milestones are joint events across stat components driven by minutes, usage and role; their probability is a tail of a covariance-aware distribution, not a product of marginals. Season-average and extreme-performance markets add a long-horizon component: availability, minutes trajectory and the variance of single-game performance.
